findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion covering test_unknown_project_fails_closed (an unknown mapped key makes compute_snapshot RAISE, never a silent empty fetch).
evidence: Testing lists 7 scenarios; AC3 says 'demonstrates all five validations' enumerating only the positive scenarios (both projects fetched, per-project resolution, preview scoping, round-trip, zero writes)
AC1 covers the read-only guard (scenario 7) but nothing covers fail-closed on an unknown mapped key
findings.finding: Scenario 6 (test_unknown_project_fails_closed) is a described deliverable in Approach ('negative-control scenario maps an UNKNOWN key and asserts the fetch FAILS CLOSED') and Testing, but no acceptance criterion covers the fail-closed behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: 'A mapping containing an unknown project key causes compute_snapshot to raise (fail-closed), verified by test_unknown_project_fails_closed passing.'

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

AC item 'An ACTUAL green live run demonstrates all five validations — both projects' cites operational evidence (live_run) that lives outside the codebase but is not tagged [operator-attested]; prefix the checkbox text with [operator-attested] so the completion verifier accepts a recorded attestation instead of failing to find code proof.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Tag AC3 and AC4 with [operator-attested] and cite a concrete attestation (run timestamp / comment id) recorded on the ticket, since their done-evidence is a live-run artifact outside the codebase.
evidence: AC3: 'the captured -rA run output is attached as a ticket comment, showing before/after Jira counts equal'
AC4: 'an aws s3 ls of the prefix returns empty, recorded on the ticket'
Scope: the CI job is a 'manually-dispatched jira-cloud-s3-rehearsal job' — not part of ordinary PR CI
findings.finding: AC3 and AC4 require done-evidence that lives OUTSIDE the codebase (a captured -rA run 'attached as a ticket comment'; an 'aws s3 ls ... recorded on the ticket') but are not tagged [operator-attested], and the live run is a manually-dispatched job not in the closing PR's CI.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefix AC3/AC4 with '[operator-attested]' and name the concrete attestation (e.g., ticket comment id + run timestamp) as the proving evidence.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the hardcoded 'total in the thousands' assertion with a robust invariant (each project > 0 and total > a small documented floor, or assert equality against a fetched count) so the test is not brittle to live-volume drift.
evidence: 'yields keys from BOTH projects at real volume (each project > 0; total in the thousands)'
The 'thousands' figure is asserted about live external data with no derivation or lower-bound rationale
findings.finding: Scenario 2 asserts 'total in the thousands' as a hardcoded volume threshold about live REB+DIG data, an asserted-not-derived expectation that will break if combined issue count drops below 1000.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert 'each project > 0 and total > N' with a small justified N (e.g. > 0 per project, > 10 total), and document that exact volume is not asserted.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the live fetch and S3 round-trip tolerate Jira Cloud rate limits and transient S3/network errors (relying on the client's existing retry/backoff, or documenting expected pagination behavior), so a green run is reproducible.
evidence: Inbound fetch drives 'per-project JQL fan-out' at 'real volume (... total in the thousands)' against live Jira Cloud
S3 round-trip: 'push the store's tickets branch to the S3 prefix, clone it back'
No mention of rate-limit handling, timeout, or retry on transient network/S3 error
findings.finding: The suite performs a live Jira Cloud fetch of large ticket volume and S3 push/clone but the plan states no timeout/retry/backoff or handling for Jira Cloud API rate limits or transient S3 failures.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note in Approach/README that the fetcher/AcliClient retry/backoff and JQL pagination are relied upon, and that transient S3 errors surface (not swallowed) with a documented rerun path.

findings.checklist_item: Reframe scenario 2's volume assertion to respect the per-query `_ACLI_CEILING` (1200) and `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` (1000): assert each project > 0 with a realistic bounded expectation (or handle SilentTruncationError explicitly), rather than a hard 'total in the thousands' floor.
evidence: Plan: 'yields keys from BOTH projects at real volume (each project > 0; total in the thousands)'
fetch_paging.py:25 `_ACLI_CEILING = 1200`; fetch_paging.py:145-150 raises SilentTruncationError(reason='ceiling') when `accumulated + len(page) >= _ACLI_CEILING` on the uncapped active query
fetcher.py:109 `_DONE_RECENT_CAP = 1000` caps the Done query per project
If REB or DIG has ~1200+ open (non-Done) issues, compute_snapshot RAISES rather than returning a snapshot, so a 'thousands' assertion fights the ceiling mechanism
findings.finding: Scenario 2 asserts a fetched 'total in the thousands', but the fetcher enforces a per-query ACLI ceiling of 1200 that RAISES SilentTruncationError (reason='ceiling') on the uncapped active query, and caps the Done query at 1000 per project — so a hard 'thousands' floor is brittle and can make the suite falsely red or non-deterministic against live volume.
findings.location: Testing → scenario 2 (test_inbound_fetch_pulls_both_projects); AC line 3 ('both projects fetched into one S3 store')
scenarios: A live project whose active working set approaches the 1200 ceiling makes compute_snapshot raise, failing the test spuriously
Even when it passes, the count is bounded near per-query ceilings, not an open-ended 'thousands'
findings.suggested_fix: Assert each project contributes > 0 keys and total is within the mechanism's bounds (≤ ~2 * (1200 + 1000) across two projects), and document that an active set near 1200 will raise SilentTruncationError by design.

findings.checklist_item: Specify that scenario 6's unknown key is SYNTACTICALLY INVALID (empty/mis-formatted) so `_validate_project_key` actually raises, or clarify which fail-closed path is being asserted vs. a valid-but-nonexistent key that returns empty.
evidence: Plan: 'an unknown mapped key makes compute_snapshot RAISE (fail-closed), never a silent empty fetch'
fetcher.py:75-87 `_validate_project_key` raises ONLY when `not project or not _PROJECT_KEY_RE.match(project)` — i.e. empty or syntactically invalid
A valid key for a non-existent project satisfies the regex, so jql_active/jql_done_recent build valid JQL and the search returns empty rather than raising
findings.finding: Scenario 6 assumes an 'unknown mapped key' makes compute_snapshot RAISE, but the fail-closed guard (_validate_project_key) only raises on a SYNTACTICALLY INVALID/empty key; a syntactically-valid-but-nonexistent project key (e.g. 'ZZZ') passes validation and issues a real JQL that returns empty — the exact 'silent empty fetch' the scenario means to preclude.
scenarios: Negative control uses a valid-looking but non-existent key -> empty snapshot, no raise -> assertion that it RAISES fails, or (worse) the test is rewritten to assert empty and no longer proves fail-closed
findings.suggested_fix: Use a key that trips `_PROJECT_KEY_RE` (e.g. '' or 'not-a-key') to guarantee the ValueError fail-closed path, and note that a syntactically-valid-but-nonexistent key returns empty rather than raising.

findings.checklist_item: Realign the leaf to parent 368f's contract — rehearse over the ephemeral Jira DC instance (file-backed store, no S3 remote) under tests/external/live_jira_dc/ per the parent's Scope — or, if the S3/Cloud approach is genuinely intended, update parent 368f first (re-staling its plan-review attestation) before re-reviewing this leaf against the corrected parent.
evidence: Parent 368f Approach: 'Rehearse against the ephemeral Jira Data Center instance ... The isolated store copy is the harness's existing local/file-based copy (REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off); no S3 remote is involved.'

Parent 368f Scope deletes 'tests/external/live_multi_project/conftest.py' and 'test_multi_project_rehearsal.py' as 'the flawed live-Cloud-only draft, replaced by the DC rehearsal'; adds files under 'tests/external/live_jira_dc/' and edits 'docs/jira-sync-setup.md'.
Parent 368f pivot comment: 'making live Cloud the wrong tier' due to two documented flaws (non-existent keys parse-ERROR; only two real Cloud projects exist).

Leaf Approach/Scope: new 'tests/external/live_jira_cloud_s3/' suite driving 'REB + DIG over an ISOLATED, S3-backed copy of the ticket store', 's3://<bucket>/<unique-prefix> wired via git-remote-s3', editing '.github/workflows/external-integration.yml' with a 'jira-cloud-s3-rehearsal' job.
Leaf AC: 'An ACTUAL green live run ... captured -rA run output is attached as a ticket comment' — a manual attested Cloud+S3 run, contradicting the parent's CI-verified DC run requirement.
findings.finding: The leaf revives the S3-backed live Jira Cloud (REB+DIG) rehearsal that its immediate parent (368f) explicitly abandoned; the parent's final, as-executed contract rehearses against the ephemeral Jira DC instance (file-backed store, no S3 remote), deletes the live-Cloud draft, and requires a green jira-dc-harness CI run — so the leaf steps entirely outside the parent's declared scope rather than narrowing it.
findings.location: Whole plan (Approach / Scope / Acceptance Criteria) vs parent 368f Description + Scope + ACs
scenarios: Leaf is claimed/reviewed against parent 368f's pinned material and diverges on tracker (Cloud vs DC), store backend (S3 vs file), files, and CI job.
Two competing rehearsal suites (live_jira_cloud_s3 vs live_jira_dc) both claim to deliver the epic's single 'Live multi-project rehearsal' child responsibility.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the AcliClient mutating-method list via find_referencing_symbols on AcliClient plus a def-sweep of acli.py, acli_rest.py, and acli_graph.py, and add the omitted public mutators (set_issue_property, set_reporter, set_relationship) — or narrow the plan's claim from 'every mutating method / STRUCTURALLY unable' to the specific methods the read paths can reach.
evidence: Plan text: 'monkeypatches every mutating method on the Cloud transport class (AcliClient.create_issue/update_issue/add_comment/add_label/remove_label/set_entity_property/delete_issue/transition_issue_by_name/unassign_issue/set_parent/update_priority/update_issuetype/update_comment/delete_comment/delete_issue_link)'
AcliClient is defined as 'class AcliClient(AcliRestMixin, AcliGraphMixin)' (acli.py:223), so mixin methods are part of its public surface

Omitted public mutators found by def-sweep: acli_rest.py:150 'def set_issue_property', acli_rest.py:168 'def set_reporter', acli_graph.py:573 'def set_relationship' — all write to Jira (REST PUT / 'link create') and none appear in the plan's list
Word 'every' in the plan asserts an exhaustive inventory, and the read-only claim is 'STRUCTURALLY unable to invoke an outbound Jira mutation'
findings.finding: The read-only guard's mutating-method inventory for AcliClient omits at least three public Jira-mutating methods that exist on the class via its mixins: set_issue_property (acli_rest.py:150), set_reporter (acli_rest.py:168), and set_relationship (acli_graph.py:573). The plan patches delete_issue_link but not set_relationship, and lists set_entity_property but not set_issue_property/set_reporter. Because the guard is asserted to be STRUCTURAL ('STRUCTURALLY unable to invoke an outbound Jira mutation'), an incomplete list leaves these public mutators callable, contradicting the claim.
findings.location: Approach — 'monkeypatches every mutating method on the Cloud transport class (AcliClient.create_issue/update_issue/add_comment/add_label/remove_label/set_entity_property/delete_issue/transition_issue_by_name/unassign_issue/set_parent/update_priority/update_issuetype/update_comment/delete_comment/delete_issue_link)'
scenarios: set_issue_property (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_rest.py:150) issues a REST PUT to /issue/{key}/properties/{key} — un-patched, so a code path invoking it would write to Jira despite the 'structural' guard
set_reporter (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_rest.py:168) issues a REST PUT editing the reporter field — un-patched mutator not covered by the guard

set_relationship (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_graph.py:573) runs 'jira workitem link create' to write an issue link — the plan patches delete_issue_link but not this create-side mutator, leaving link creation reachable
findings.suggested_fix: Add set_issue_property, set_reporter, and set_relationship to the monkeypatched set, and derive the full list from the class MRO (AcliClient + AcliRestMixin + AcliGraphMixin) rather than a hand list; also grep for any string-based dispatch (getattr/monkeypatch.setattr by name) to catch dynamically referenced mutators the LSP will not surface.
